scenario.captureCommand: env -i HOME=$HOME USER=$USER LANG=en_US.UTF-8 PATH=<node-bin>:/usr/bin:/bin <real-claude-binary> -p "$PROMPT" --model claude-haiku-4-5 --output-format stream-json --verbose --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources "" --disable-slash-commands --allowedTools Bash --permission-mode acceptEdits  (see scripts/windows-port/capture-claude-stream-json-golden.sh)
scenario.description: A real, authenticated `claude --output-format stream-json` run on macOS (Claude Code 2.1.191), invoking the genuine claude binary directly (not the cmux wrapper shim) in a stripped env with --setting-sources "" + --disable-slash-commands + --strict-mcp-config so the system/init line is canonical (no personal skills/plugins/MCP servers). The marker-file scenario forces one Bash tool_use + tool_result, so the raw stream exercises system/init, a rate_limit_event, system/thinking_tokens, assistant thinking, assistant tool_use, user tool_result, assistant text, and the final result-with-usage. The shipped ClaudeCodeStreamJSONParser projects this raw stream to exactly the events below (toolUse + toolResult + text — the complete reachable set for this parser); it does not emit reasoning/usage for Claude, which is faithful production behavior (usage arrives on the raw result line, harvested by the log/quota path, not the live stream parser). The committed raw carries one deterministic, event-neutral PII redaction: the local macOS home path was rewritten to /Users/openburnbar in the inert system/init memory_paths field, which the parser never reads (zero parsed-event impact — proven by re-parsing the committed raw).
scenario.prompt: There is a file named marker.txt in the current working directory. Use the Bash tool to run: cat marker.txt — to read its contents. Then reply with ONLY the exact one-line contents of that file and nothing else. Do not guess; you must actually run the command to learn the value.
